piTests: packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts:records how long execute() took on the tool result, excluding hooks
rows.notes: Frozen durationMs is measured with perf.now around execute only (after prepareArguments, beforeToolCall and before afterToolCall): a 120 ms before hook plus 10 ms execute produced durationMs=10 and wallClock=121. Frozen end event and tool-result message carry durationMs only for executed calls; blocked/unknown/truncated lack the key. C++ ToolExecutionEndEvent and ToolResultMessage have no duration; only NestedToolCallRecord.duration_ms exists. This is the central acceptance gap.

piTests: packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts:declares tool loadout changes and resolves calls against the executable set
rows.notes: Frozen state.tools is the executable set: assignment copies the replacement array, a removed tool call returns "Tool a not found" and never executes, and the next request receives a system message declaring toolsAdded/toolsRemoved. C++ set_active_tools only narrows the declared snapshot; ToolCallExecutor resolves every call against the full registry, so an inactive tool still executes and no system tool-delta message is emitted. Later C++ test must assert execute count 0 for the removed name, not only that the prompt declaration hides it.

excluded.reason: Explicitly excluded by #1047: the streamProxy protocol is a separate pi-ai/AI audit, not an Agent execution observation.
Assistant message_update/thinking/message timing belongs to the AI stream audit; #1047 captures only ordinary stream injection into Agent lifecycle ordering.
Provider retry, transport selection, thinkingBudgets and onPayload/onResponse hooks are AI/provider behavior, not Agent tool execution or queue admission.
ToolResultMessage.usage is an AI message-shape concern; #1047 records only the Agent-owned duration field and result outcome.

The frozen coding-agent concrete tools (read/bash/edit/write) live in the cch_coding_agent-owned harness layer, not in this ticket's cch_agent_core package. Recording the required target/ownership gap does not authorize a move in an audit.

gaps.statement: ToolExecutionEndEvent and ToolResultMessage have no durationMs; AgentSession/ProjectionStream cannot carry it.
gaps.required: Measure monotonic execute-only duration after prepareArguments/beforeToolCall and before afterToolCall; attach it to the end event and the executed tool-result message; omit it for blocked/unknown/truncated calls.

gaps.statement: MessageDto/SessionMessageJson lacks durationMs, so the session record cannot round-trip the frozen field.
gaps.required: Add optional durationMs to ToolResultMessage and MessageDto serialize/deserialize without inventing it for absent calls.
evidence: fixtures/pi-v1.3.0/audit-1047/tool-execution.json:tool duration survives the public session record round trip

gaps.statement: ToolExecutionComponent/BashRenderer derive the visible duration from wall-clock start/end timestamps, not the frozen monotonic execute-only duration.
gaps.required: Consume the event/result duration or prove the visible timer is intentionally non-contract; add a discriminating test with a long hook and short execute.

gaps.statement: C++ has no ToolDefinition.prepareArguments hook; raw model arguments are validated before any normalization.
gaps.required: Run prepareArguments before validation and beforeToolCall, preserving the no-revalidation contract for hook mutations.
evidence: fixtures/pi-v1.3.0/audit-1047/tool-execution.json:prepareArguments runs before validation and beforeToolCall mutations execute without revalidation

gaps.statement: Tool::concurrency defaults to Exclusive although the header documents ParallelSafe as the omitted default and frozen pi runs omitted executionMode concurrently.
gaps.required: Default to ParallelSafe (or otherwise preserve per-tool sequential overrides and the batch sequential rule) and add a concurrency test.
evidence: fixtures/pi-v1.3.0/audit-1047/tool-execution.json:parallel tool ends follow completion order while result messages keep source order
